html:
SMTO-HTTP-0010 — This task has connected to too many web services

GUID: fe90bd4a-79ff-4420-9000-1fb33b325882
Slug: http-connection-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • One task can keep up to 32 different web service connections, and this task has used them all. The new connection wasn't made; work already done in this task is unaffected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to reuse a connection it already made in this task for the same service instead of setting up a new one. A connection with exactly the same settings reuses its existing slot, so it doesn't count against the limit.
  2. If the task really needs more services, let the current task finish (or select Stop), then select New chat and ask for the remaining work there. The limit counts connections per task, so a new task starts with an empty list.
  3. For big jobs that touch many different services, ask for them in several smaller requests instead of one large one. Each smaller task stays well under the 32-connection limit.

What success looks like

  • SMTO continues using an existing connection, or the new task connects to the service without showing this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to skip its connection safety checks to fit more in; the limit protects which services a task can reach.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HttpConnections.capture refused a new connection recipe because this run already holds 32 distinct recipes and none matches the requested profile, Gateway and origin.

What this means

  • The run already retains 32 distinct connection recipes and the requested recipe does not match one that can be reused. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The run already retains 32 distinct connection recipes and the requested recipe does not match one that can be reused.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current recipes and exact reusable connections; the registry has no automatic expiry/removal path that frees this bound.

How to fix it

  • HttpConnections.capture (src/agent_runtime/native/http_connections.py) caps each run at 32 distinct connection recipes; a recipe identical to an existing one reuses its reference. Reuse an existing connection_ref from the current run, or settle this run and make the additional connections from a new run; do not raise or bypass the limit.
  • Reuse an appropriate current connection; if distinct additional connections are necessary, settle this run and start a new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Work uses a matching existing connection, or separately authorized new work starts in a fresh run.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
